At its current price, AbbVie would need to grow revenue about 16.6% a year for five years merely to maintain its share price, offering no return on top. At a steady net margin of 16.1%, that profit would take revenue of $142 billion by fiscal Q3 2031. That margin is just above AbbVie’s best twelve-month net margin of 15.7% over the last twelve quarter-ends, and well above the 8.5% average over that span. The revenue needed is more than double the $66.0 billion AbbVie reported over the past twelve months. Trefis allows five years because today’s P/E is more than twice the mature one. Skyrizi sold $17.6 billion in fiscal 2025, and management expects $21.8 billion for fiscal 2026; Rinvoq sold $8.3 billion in fiscal 2025, and management expects $10.3 billion for fiscal 2026. If AbbVie’s P/E settled to the mature level in three years, the company would have to grow revenue 29.2% a year. Given seven years, it would need 11.6%. So how expensive AbbVie looks depends on how long you expect its multiple to stay high. AbbVie is also starting from its best recent figures. Its revenue growth over the past twelve months was its fastest of the last five twelve-month periods, and its twelve-month net margin was 4.0% a year earlier. The requirement assumes AbbVie keeps its net margin a little above its recent high and lifts revenue growth well above its recent pace. Based on today’s figures, AbbVie stock is expensive: the business would have to grow faster than in any recent year simply for the price to hold. Achieving that pace requires Skyrizi and Rinvoq to grow fast enough to more than replace Humira, with the net margin kept near its recent high. AbbVie ABBV announced encouraging third-quarter 2026 results last month, which beat expectations for both earnings and sales. The company's immunology revenues increased 16.6% year over year on an operational basis to approximately $9.2 billion. The figure accounted for nearly 53% of total revenues. Strong sales of its two blockbuster drugs, Rinvoq and Skyrizi, helped offset the continued erosion of legacy drug Humira and reinforced their importance as AbbVie's key long-term growth drivers. Skyrizi sales jumped 22.9% year over year on an operational basis to $5.8 billion, while Rinvoq revenues increased 24.3% to $2.7 billion. Both drugs benefited from strong demand and market-share gains across their approved indications, particularly in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), which includes ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD). In contrast, Humira sales declined 30.6% year over year to $683 million due to continued biosimilar competition. Strong momentum across its immunology franchise also supported AbbVie's improved 2026 outlook. The company raised its sales forecasts for both drugs. It now expects Skyrizi sales of $21.8 billion and Rinvoq sales of approximately $10.3 billion. Combined, the two drugs are expected to deliver more than 20% growth in 2026. Overall immunology revenues are forecast at approximately $34.9 billion. New indications are expected to provide further growth opportunities. Skyrizi recently received FDA approval for a subcutaneous induction regimen for CD, offering patients a more convenient treatment option. Management expects payer access to expand over approximately 60 days, with the benefits likely to become more visible in early 2027. Meanwhile, Rinvoq is expanding its presence in dermatology, with commercialization for vitiligo and alopecia areata underway in Europe. U.S. regulatory decisions for both indications are anticipated over the coming months. AbbVie expects the two indications to generate nearly $2 billion in combined peak sales. The immunology market is highly competitive, with major pharmaceutical companies vying for market share across several indications. A key competitor is Johnson & Johnson JNJ, which markets two major immunology drugs, Stelara and Tremfya. Both drugs are approved for multiple inflammatory conditions, including UC and CD. Following the entry of Stelara biosimilars in the United States in 2025, J&J is increasingly relying on Tremfya's growth to offset declining Stelara sales and support its immunology franchise. J&J is also expanding its immunology portfolio. Earlier in March, it secured approval for Icotyde, a once-daily oral drug for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. While still in the early stages of launch, the drug poses a competitive threat to Skyrizi. Eli Lilly LLY is another competitor expanding its presence in immunology through Omvoh. The drug received FDA approval for UC in October 2023 and for CD in January 2025. These approvals established the LLY drug as a competitor in both major forms of IBD, where AbbVie's Skyrizi has been gaining traction. Year to date, shares of AbbVie have risen 29% compared with the industry's 26% growth. From a valuation standpoint, AbbVie is trading at a slight discount to the industry. title: AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) Leads Analyst Picks As NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Trails Its Semiconductor Peers - Foreign Policy Journal
content: By David Prior | Nov 12, 2026 | Economy & Business, Featured, News & Analysis AbbVie Inc. (NYSE: ABBV) has emerged as one of the standout performers in the latest round of analyst coverage, surging 41.4% over six months against a 28.4% gain for the broader Medical-Products industry. Analysts credit AbbVie’s relative strength to the successful commercial ramp of Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which have meaningfully cushioned the revenue erosion left by Humira’s patent expiration. An expanding neuroscience portfolio, a pipeline of new indication approvals, and targeted strategic acquisitions are seen as the pillars supporting AbbVie’s longer-term growth trajectory. That said, Humira’s continuing decline, softening oncology revenues, and macroeconomic headwinds weighing on the company’s Aesthetics division are flagged as risks that investors cannot afford to ignore. The contrast with NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA) is striking, as the chipmaker’s shares have lagged the Zacks Semiconductor-General industry over the past year, falling 12.9% against the industry’s 3.7% decline. Chinese regulatory restrictions on data center sales, customer concentration risk, and rising capital commitments are cited as the primary drags on NVIDIA’s near-term outlook. Analysts do note, however, that broad AI infrastructure spending, adoption of the Blackwell Ultra architecture, and the rollout of the Vera Rubin platform give NVIDIA credible long-term growth levers. Walmart Inc. (NYSE: WMT) presents a more straightforward story, outpacing the Retail-Supermarkets industry over the past year with a 21.4% gain versus the sector’s 20.4% advance. The retailer’s omnichannel model, growing advertising and membership revenue streams, and continued e-commerce momentum are viewed as durable competitive advantages that underpin its premium valuation. Analysts flag elevated operating costs, pharmacy-related sales headwinds, and the potential margin drag from ongoing price investments as the key risks to Walmart’s profitability outlook. Among micro-cap names covered in the same research batch, Pioneer Bancorp Inc. (NASDAQ: PBFS) has outrun the Banks-Northeast peer group by a wide margin, delivering a 37.7% return over the past year versus the industry’s 27.2%. Wider net interest spreads, loan and deposit growth, and an expansion into specialty finance are identified as the drivers behind Pioneer’s outperformance, though acquisition costs and rising charge-offs remain concerns. Aspira Women’s Health Inc. (NASDAQ: AWHL) sits at the opposite end of the performance spectrum, having lost 66.6% over the past year while the Medical-Instruments industry gained 24.5%. Analysts describe Aspira’s investment case as highly execution-dependent, with liquidity constraints and commercialization uncertainty representing substantial hurdles, even as the ENDOinform product targets an underserved clinical market. The Cleveland Clinic partnership and an established distribution network are cited as genuine assets that could support future launches if management is able to stabilize the core business. Elsewhere in Wednesday’s research output, General Dynamics received a positive note tied to growing Pentagon and allied-nation orders, while Morgan Stanley was highlighted for its investment banking strength and strategic acquisition activity. On the ratings front, Humana and Super Micro were among the names receiving upgrades, while D.R. Horton, Construction Partners, and Ingredion were all downgraded on concerns ranging from mortgage affordability to input cost inflation. title: Could AbbVie Stock Survive A Skyrizi And Rinvoq Slowdown? - Trefis

Skyrizi and Rinvoq are AbbVie’s (ABBV) two biggest drugs, and a slowdown in them is the risk a holder should weigh. Together they made up about 42% of AbbVie’s revenue in 2025. The worry is not idle: on its October 30, 2026 call, management said the pair has been on the market for 8 years and faces more competition, though it made that point to stress that both are still growing fast. The same day, AbbVie reported revenue that rose on strength in immunology and neuroscience. So has that competition started to slow either drug? Not in the latest quarter. In fiscal Q3 2026, Skyrizi sales reached nearly $5.8 billion, up 22.9% on an operational basis. Rinvoq grew faster still, posting sales of $2.7 billion, up 24.3%. Management said recent oral competition is not having a substantive impact on Skyrizi in psoriasis, where the drug still wins roughly 1 out of every 2 new or switching patients. AbbVie also raised its full-year Skyrizi sales guidance for the third time in 2026. AbbVie has seen what happens when competition does take hold. Humira sales were $683 million in the quarter, down 30.6% on an operational basis, which management put down to continued competition from biosimilars, close copies of the drug. Management expects about $67.8 billion of revenue for 2026, compared with the $61.2 billion reported for 2025. Of that $6.6 billion rise, management says Skyrizi and Rinvoq are adding $6 billion. Vraylar is growing too, but shrinking sales for Humira and Imbruvica leave the two biggest drugs to generate most of the net gain. A slowdown in the two drugs would therefore show up first as slower revenue growth for AbbVie, not as lower total sales. That growth matters for the price you pay: AbbVie stock trades at 7.9 times its sales, against 3.2 for the S&P 500, which suggests buyers are paying for growth. Separately from the two drugs, the stock has fallen in past market shocks, though by very different amounts. During the 2023 SVB regional banking crisis, AbbVie stock fell 13.0%, while the S&P 500 fell 6.7%. In the 2025 US tariff shock, the stock fell by the same 13.0%, against 19.0% for the S&P 500. In the 2022 inflation shock and the 2023 bond yield shock, it fell just 1.5% and 1.9%, against 24.0% and 9.5% for the S&P 500. AbbVie has absorbed a large drug’s decline before, but only through growth in these same two drugs. Humira sales fell to $4.54 billion in 2025, from $8.99 billion in 2024. AbbVie’s total revenue still rose that year, from $56.3 billion in 2024 to $61.2 billion. Over the same year, Skyrizi sales grew to $17.6 billion from $11.7 billion, and Rinvoq’s to $8.3 billion from $5.97 billion, together more than the whole rise in revenue. The company also has cash to work with. Free cash flow, the cash left after capital spending, was $18.9 billion over the twelve months to September 30, 2026. Over the same period, operating income was 8.0 times interest expense. Against that, AbbVie carries $70.1 billion of debt net of its cash. For shareholders, the growth of these two drugs has to hold. The quarterly sales growth for Skyrizi and Rinvoq is the measure to watch in AbbVie’s fiscal Q4 2026 report, expected in February 2027. Management also plans to give its 2027 guidance at that time. AbbVie's ABBV stock has risen 4.5% in a month, mainly driven by its robust third-quarter performance. Third-quarter adjusted earnings per share of $3.82 surpassed management's guidance and surged 105.4% year over year. Total net revenues were $17.4 billion, beating the company's expectations by $200 million and reflecting robust sales growth of more than 10%. AbbVie's nine products delivered double-digit growth. Based on the strong performance across its business, including Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Vraylar, Ubrelvy, Qulipta and Venclexta, AbbVie raised its revenue guidance for the third time this year. Total revenues are expected to be $67.8 billion in 2026, up from the prior expectation of $67.6 billion. The company has now raised its annual revenue guidance by a cumulative $800 million since the beginning of 2026. However, a single quarter's results are not so important for long-term investors, and the focus should rather be on the company's strong fundamentals. Let's understand the company's strengths and weaknesses to better analyze how to play AbbVie stock. Sales of Humira, a drug that once generated more than 50% of AbbVie's total revenues, are declining due to loss of exclusivity (LOE) and biosimilar erosion. However, AbbVie has successfully navigated the Humira LOE period by launching two other successful immunology medicines, Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which are performing extremely well, bolstered by approvals in new indications, and should support top-line growth in the next few years. While Skyrizi sales rose 22.9% on an operational basis to $5.78 billion in the third quarter, Rinvoq sales increased 24.3% to $2.71 billion. In 2026, AbbVie expects combined Skyrizi and Rinvoq sales of more than $32 billion, representing potential growth of more than 20%. It has already recorded $23.1 billion in sales in the first nine months of 2026. Strong immunology market growth, market share gains and momentum from new indications are expected to drive these drugs' growth. Rinvoq was approved for two indications — vitiligo and alopecia areata — in the EU in July 2026, while applications are under review in the United States. In addition, phase III data for Rinvoq in hidradenitis suppurativa and systemic lupus erythematosus are expected in 2026. AbbVie believes that the vitiligo and alopecia areata indications alone can add up to $2 billion in combined peak sales for Rinvoq. AbbVie is evaluating Skyrizi-based combination regimens with assets like ABBV-382 (anti-α4β7) and ABBV-701 (anti-TL1A) to create best-in-class, durable remission therapies in IBD. It gained FDA approval for a subcutaneous induction regimen for Skyrizi in Crohn's disease in October, which can improve the drug's competitive positioning and drive an acceleration in sales. However, the March 2026 launch of J&J's JNJ new oral IL-23 receptor inhibitor, Icotyde (icotrokinra), for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis has intensified competition for Skyrizi. Icotyde's convenient oral administration could affect Skyrizi's prescription trends and market share over time. However, on the third-quarter conference call, AbbVie said that it has not seen any "substantive impact" in Skyrizi's momentum despite competition from J&J's Icotyde. AbbVie's neuroscience portfolio is also contributing to top-line growth, driven by higher sales of Botox Therapeutic, depression drug Vraylar, newer migraine drugs Ubrelvy and Qulipta, and new Parkinson's disease drug, Vyalev. AbbVie's oral CGRPs, Ubrelvy and Qulipta/Aquipta, represent a combined $5 billion-plus peak sales opportunity. The launch of Vyalev, a transformative therapy for treating advanced Parkinson's disease, approved in late 2024, has been encouraging, with first nine months 2026 sales reaching $743 million. AbbVie expects the therapy to achieve blockbuster status in 2026 as U.S. uptake accelerates following full coverage. AbbVie's once-daily oral tablet, Juvmo (tavapadon), was approved by the FDA for treating Parkinson's disease in September 2026. With Juvmo, Vyalev and Duopa, AbbVie expects its Parkinson's disease franchise to have peak annual sales potential of more than $5 billion and to be a key neuroscience growth driver. AbbVie boasts a robust pipeline. Last month, AbbVie announced positive top-line data from the phase III INTREPID study evaluating its investigational drug, lutikizumab, in adults and adolescents with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa (HS). The study met its primary endpoint, with 31.4% of patients receiving lutikizumab achieving Hidradenitis Suppurativa Clinical Response 75 (HiSCR75) at week 16 compared with 23.4% on placebo. Lutikizumab also met eight ranked secondary endpoints, demonstrating significant improvements in HS-related skin pain and reductions in disease flares. Last month, it also submitted a biologics license application (BLA) to the FDA seeking approval of etentamig, a BCMA CD3 bispecific developed for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. In May, the FDA approved Decnupaz/pivekimab sunirine for blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm in the United States, and as discussed before, Juvmo was approved by the FDA in September. These new products/pipeline programs have the potential to drive long-term growth for AbbVie, while Skyrizi and Rinvoq should boost near-term growth. AbbVie has also been on an acquisition spree over the past couple of years to bolster the early-stage pipeline that should drive long-term growth. It is signing several M&A deals in the immunology space, its core area, while also signing some early-stage deals in oncology and neuroscience. The acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics in 2026 added promising dermatology, respiratory and inflammatory disease assets that have strengthened its immunology pipeline and support long-term growth. AbbVie has been witnessing weak sales in its aesthetics segment for the past couple of years. Persistent macroeconomic challenges, inflationary pressures and subdued consumer confidence, particularly in the United States, continue to weigh on discretionary spending and aesthetics sales. Juvederm sales declined 7.2% in the first nine months of 2026 on an operational basis, while Botox Cosmetic rose 7.6% due to improving market growth. Although the aesthetics market is showing early signs of stabilization after several quarters of weakness, challenges persist. The company expects global aesthetics sales of $5 billion in 2026, flat from 2025 levels, as moderate growth in Botox Cosmetic is likely to be offset by continued weakness in Juvederm due to headwinds in key dermal filler markets. Sales of Humira are declining due to biosimilar erosion. The launch of Humira biosimilars in the United States in 2023 has significantly eroded the drug's sales since 2024. Humira sales declined 35.9% on an operational basis in the first nine months of 2026 and are likely to decline in future quarters. AbbVie has established a substantial oncology franchise with Imbruvica and Venclexta, complemented by newer drugs like Elahere, Epkinly and Emrelis. However, oncology sales growth remains subdued, as higher Venclexta sales and growing contributions from newer drugs are being largely offset by declining Imbruvica sales. AbbVie's oncology sales declined 1.5% on an operational basis in the first nine months of 2026. However, AbbVie believes the oncology pipeline is robust, with several study readouts and initiations expected in the next few months. ABBV stock has risen 28.6% so far this year compared with an increase of 25.5% for the industry. From a valuation standpoint, AbbVie is reasonably priced. Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 18.67 forward earnings, lower than 19.83 for the industry. However, the stock is trading above its five-year mean of 14.22. The stock is cheaper than other large drugmakers like Eli Lilly LLY, J&J and Gilead GILD. Earnings estimates for 2026 have been stable at $13.97 over the past 30 days, while those for 2027 have risen from $15.95 to $16.02 over the same time frame. AbbVie combats its share of headwinds, including the impact of Humira LOE, slowing oncology sales, evolving competitive dynamics for Skyrizi and continued macro woes for Aesthetics. However, despite Humira's U.S. patent expiry, AbbVie has successfully offset much of the blockbuster's lost revenues with strong sales of Skyrizi and Rinvoq, easing concerns over its long-term earnings outlook. Strong momentum in its neuroscience portfolio, particularly its migraine and Parkinson's disease drugs, and a promising pipeline further strengthen its prospects. AbbVie expects total revenues to rise around 10% in 2026, backed mainly by significant momentum in immunology and neuroscience products, which are demonstrating significant growth and delivering share gains in growing markets. It expects high single-digit revenue growth through 2029. Investors should retain this Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) stock given its resilient core business, expanding portfolio and solid long-term prospects.
